summary: Magdalena department stands under the national framework of Colombia. No department-specific trans finding was identified for Magdalena in the source inventory; the national assessment applies.
tangentialFactors:
National reporting on attacks against LGBTQ+ people in Colombia after the killing of Sara Millerey (CNN, 6 August 2025) contains no information specific to Magdalena.

A Guardian investigation of 30 July 2024 reports that armed groups in Caquetá gave trans woman Tatiana Cespedes one week to leave town or be killed and circulated 'social cleansing' flyers against trans women. It quotes an activist stating that the prosecutor's office does not recognise transfemicide, recording the killings as ordinary cases. Colombia recorded 41 trans women killed in 2023 and eight between February and April 2024. These national figures are the baseline against which Magdalena is assessed; the investigation provides no Magdalena-specific information.

Colombian society is described as generally conservative on LGBT issues; an Invamer poll of October 2019 recorded 50% support for same-sex marriage for the first time, with 47% opposed.
localsOnly:
Consensual same-sex activity has been legal in Colombia since 1981, and Congress passed a law banning discrimination based on sexual orientation in 2011. The right to change legal gender has existed since 1993, and since 2015 gender change has been possible without psychiatric or physical evaluations.

The Constitutional Court legalized same-sex marriage in April 2016, making Colombia the fourth Latin American country to do so, and granted same-sex couples full adoption rights in 2015. Transgender people have been allowed to serve openly in the military since 2015.
